newsitem.title: UK: Britain cool on extra Euro-summit.
newsitem.headline: Britain cool on extra Euro-summit.

text.p: Britain on Sunday made clear its lack of enthusiasm for an extra European Union summit scheduled to be held just days before the ruling Conservative Party, deeply split over Europe, holds its annual conference.
EU ministers meeting in Ireland over the weekend set October 5 as the date for the extra summit, just three days before the Conservative conference.

The Dublin government, which currently holds the rotating EU presidency, has been asked to hold the meeting to review the progress of talks by a standing inter-governmental conference (IGC) to discuss a revision of the EU's founding treaties.
The review is supposed to be finished by the middle of next year to streamline the EU for the 21st century and an influx of countries from eastern Europe.
But British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said he was not "overwhelmed with enthusiasm" at the prospect of an extra EU summit.

Speaking in London during talks with Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy, Rifkind said some of the EU foreign ministers meeting at Tralee questioned whether the timing of the meeting was entirely appropriate.

"We are very relaxed about it. If there is work to be done, if there are views that could be properly expressed and possible conclusions reached, let's go ahead with it. But if there is a general consensus that it may not be necessary, I don't think we will lose too many tears."
Britain's relationship with Europe has opened deep splits in the Conservatives, with Major struggling to maintain party discipline with a parliamentary majority of just one seat.
Major must call a general election by next May and the party conference will be crucial in rallying his forces for a gruelling election campaign.
